geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the blunt notch with a split-wing mass to generate a clearer dominant body and a more legible public threshold on the access side.
Use the long axis split to reinforce the bar-like neighborhood-living brief and preserve a strong primary mass.
Create a modest but readable separation so the void becomes public and not merely incidental.
Maintain a continuous grounded connector so the split remains one compositional rule rather than two colliding solids.
Keep the upper connection readable so the silhouette preserves hierarchy while acknowledging the void.

graph_edits.rationale: The current notch reads as a sealed clipped object; reframe the primary mass as a split-wing condition to create a clearer dominant body with a meaningful ground threshold.
Keep the primary articulation aligned to the verified access side so the threshold responds to frontage rather than turning away from it.
Widen the carved opening so the access response reads as a legible public void instead of a small bite.
Reduce the vertical reach of the notch so the cut operates as a grounded entry/court condition rather than a top-heavy clip.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact prismatic mass with one main dominant body, but the four-view set shows an awkwardly clipped/notched object whose spatial logic is not fully coherent across views. The access edge is not convincingly answered by a public void or clear threshold; instead the ground response feels mostly sealed, with the carved condition reading more like a geometric bite than a meaningful entry court. The silhouette is not stair-like in a positive sectional sense, but the stepped/angled faces do not yet resolve into a continuous, capacity-bearing section. Programmatically, a neighborhood-living mixed-use building needs an active ground edge and legible public threshold; this candidate is too close to a generic object mass with a weak street relationship and insufficient section/public-space logic. Reference language suggests a clearer dominant mass and more intentional frontage articulation, but the current form does not yet carry that into a credible massing diagram.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more tower-like than the neighborhood-living brief; do not copy the tower typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered mass with a legible continuous datum; useful as a precedent for a more coherent upper-mass hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office tower typology and river-context image are only loosely relevant to a compact street building.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single tall volume with a subtly torqued or softened profile can create one clear dominant gesture.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Restaurant/cafe frontage is useful only as a frontage-response precedent; the overall building type is not aligned.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low horizontal base with a distinct entry/canopy read and a calmer upper datum.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the visible views, but the mass is still weak on access-edge response.
Solids do not visibly collide; the main failure is semantic/sectional coherence rather than a hard geometric clash.
